The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
On 15.10.2023 at about 3.15 p.m., the petitioner was SCCH - 26 3 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 riding the Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-51-HR-9739 by following the traffic rules and regulations and also wearing helmet.

When he was proceeding opposite Radiant Resort, C.K. Palya, Bangalore, at that time the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EW-6696 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger to the public and dashed to the petitioner's scooter.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to whole body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Vijayashree Hospital, Bangalore after first aid he was shifted to Fortis Hospital, BG road, Bangalore wherein x-rays were taken and underwent operations internal implants were fixed, he was treated with surgery as inpatient for 4 days and discharged on 18-10-2023 with an advice to under continuous follow-up treatment and complete bed rest and he has spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical treatment, hospitalization,
conveyance, attendant and other incidental expenses.
SCCH - 26 4 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 4.
Prior to the accident petitioner was aged about 78 years, he was hale and healthy, he was a business man getting income of Rs.22,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, he is still under treatment bound to bed and could not resume his avocation till the date.

sentences.text: The Hulimavu traffic Police has registered the case in Cr.No.160/2023 against the driver of offending motor cycle under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.

The accident was occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving of driver of 1 st respondent and the policy was valid at the time of accident and the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AG-5744 was holding valid driving licence.
Hence the respondent No.3 is liable to pay compensation.
Accordingly, the petitioner has prayed to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- together with cost and interest.
6. After service of summons, respondent No.1 and 2 remained absent and they are placed Ex-parte.
Respondent No.3 appeared through its counsels and filed objection statement.
Respondent No.3 in its objection statement contending that, the motor cycle bearing NO.KA-51-EW-6696 is having valid insurance policy.
The owner of the vehicle knowing fully entrusted to drive the vehicle, which does not possess valid and effective driving licence.
There is violation of Section 158(b) and 134(c) of MV Act.

There is no negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-51-EW-6696 and the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the scooter bearing reg.No.KA-51-HR-9739.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further denied the disability sustained by the petitioner, occupation and income of the petitioner and the registration of criminal case against the driver of above said motor cycle.
For all these reasons, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

8. On the basis of the above pleadings, following issues have been framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on SCCH - 26 6 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 15-10-2023 at about 3.15 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in his scooter bearing reg.No.KA-51-HR- 9739 opposite Radiant resort, C.K.Palya, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-51-EW-6696 rode in a high speed and negligent manner and dashed against him.
Due to this, accident occurred and petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition? If so, from which respondent?
3. What Order or award?

On perusal of Ex.P.2, complaint it reveals that petitioner has lodged the complaint and on the basis of the said complaint, Hulimavu traffic Police have registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 against the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-EW-6696.

16. All the records indicate the negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-EW-6696.
Respondents No.3 has failed to prove the allegations of the petitioner with regard to the injury sustained by him in the alleged accident due to rash and negligent riding of offending motor cycle.

By the above materials and evidence it is clear that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-EW-6696 by its rider.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner has produced his Aadhaar Card as per Ex.P.19 to consider his age at the time of accident.

In Ex.P.11, the date of birth of petitioner SCCH - 26 11 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 is mentioned as 15.01.1945, the accident was occurred on 15-10-2023, hence the age of petitioner is considered as 78 years at the time of accident.

Therefore by considering the evidence on record and opinion of the doctor, I am of the opinion that, the disability of the petitioner has to be taking into consideration for his physical disability to award compensation.
So, in view of all these circumstances, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
18. In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was doing business and earning a sum of Rs.22,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the respondent No.3 has denied the profession and income of petitioner.
The petitioner has not produced his Bank Statement or any documents to show that, he was doing business and earning Rs.22,000/- p.m.
Hence it appears that, except the oral version of PW1, nothing is available on record to consider the avocation and income of the petitioner as stated by him.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision of Yashoda.H and others V/s. Sharath Kumar Achar and another.

23. Petitioner has also examined Dr.Ramesh.B, Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.P.20 and Ex.P.21.
P.W.2 has filed affidavit evidence in lieu of examination in chief and he has deposed that, on 29-4- 2025, he examined the petitioner for disability assessment.

Finally P.W.2 has deposed that,
the SCCH - 26 15 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 petitioner suffers from permanent physical disability of 22%

sentences.text: By careful perusal of the entire cross-examination of P.W.2, it can be inferred that, he is not the treated doctor.
As such, this Tribunal is declined to consider the entire evidence of P.W.2.

It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

But in the present case, though the petitioner has got examined the doctor as PW.2 to show his disability and the documents placed on record shows that he has the permanent physical disability at 22% of right lower limb which is 11% to the whole body.
But by looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed SCCH - 26 16 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
The petitioner has got examined one Raghu Y.C.-Medical record officer at Fortis hospital as PW-3 who has produced Ex.P22- authorisation letter and Ex.P23-case sheet.
The petitioner is aged about 78 years and he has not undergone surgery.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 8% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
25. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned, considering the fact that the Petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and in total he was inpatient for a period of 4 days in total which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain.
Hence, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.40,000/- would be just and proper compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
26. LOSS OF AMENITIES:- Further on perusal of evidence of PW.1, it reveals that, petitioner has sustained injuries and the same is mentioned above paras.
The petitioner was aged about 78 years at the time of accident.

Considering the above facts and on perusal of evidence of SCCH - 26 17 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 PW.1 and PW.2 and also considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.
27. ATTENDANT, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
As per discharge summary produced at Ex.P.13, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Fortis Hospital from 15-10-2023 to 18-10-2023 for a period of 4 days.
The petitioner is aged about 78 years, he might have age old sufferings and he might have taken assistance from attender.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of Rs.6,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.

28. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As on the date of accident he was aged about 78 years.
Therefore, the appropriate multiplier for the said age group as per Sarla Verma's case is '5'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for the SCCH - 26 18 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 compensation of Rs.76,800/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 5 X 8/100)
towards loss of future income on the account of disability of the petitioner.

The petitioner has not produced any evidence to show that, he has taken follow-up treatment.

By considering 4 days as inpatient and follow up treatment taken by the petitioner on several occasions, around 02 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for two months.

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
34. The Respondent No.1 is the RC owner of offending motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-51-EW-6696 and Respondent No.3 is the insurer.
Hence, both the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to the compensation to the Petitioner.

However, the respondent No.3 being the insurer of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EW-6696 is liable to pay compensation Rs. 4,27,430/-
with 6% interest to the petitioner from the date of petition till deposit the amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the 'partly affirmative'.

O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  SCCH - 26 21 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 compensation of Rs. 4,27,430/- (Rupees four lakhs twenty seven thousand four hundred and thirty Only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 & 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, the respondent No.3 being insurer of offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 51-EW-6696 is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount, release the entire amount to the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

: 
The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
When he was proceeding opposite Radiant Resort, C.K. Palya, Bangalore, at that time the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EW-6696 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger to the public and dashed to the petitioner's scooter.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to whole body.
The Hulimavu traffic Police has registered the case in Cr.No.160/2023 against the driver of offending motor cycle under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
The accident was occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving of driver of 1 st respondent and the policy was valid at the time of accident and the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AG-5744 was holding valid driving licence.
Hence the respondent No.3 is liable to pay compensation.
The owner of the vehicle knowing fully entrusted to drive the vehicle, which does not possess valid and effective driving licence.
There is violation of Section 158(b) and 134(c) of MV Act.
There is no negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-51-EW-6696 and the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the scooter bearing reg.No.KA-51-HR-9739.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further denied the disability sustained by the petitioner, occupation and income of the petitioner and the registration of criminal case against the driver of above said motor cycle.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
18. In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was doing business and earning a sum of Rs.22,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the respondent No.3 has denied the profession and income of petitioner.
The petitioner has not produced his Bank Statement or any documents to show that, he was doing business and earning Rs.22,000/- p.m.
Hence it appears that, except the oral version of PW1, nothing is available on record to consider the avocation and income of the petitioner as stated by him.
In this case, the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the SCCH - 26 12 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 notional income as fixed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore, in view of the above decision and the accident was occurred during the year 2023, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
But in the present case, though the petitioner has got examined the doctor as PW.2 to show his disability and the documents placed on record shows that he has the permanent physical disability at 22% of right lower limb which is 11% to the whole body.
But by looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed SCCH - 26 16 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of Rs.6,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The petitioner became a disabled and unable to do his work as he was doing prior to the accident and sustained loss of future earnings.
Per contra learned counsel for respondent No.3 has vehemently argued that, the petitioner was sustained simple injuries, as per wound certificate and disability does not arise.
The petitioner was suffering s from age old pains.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence the petitioner is entitled for the SCCH - 26 18 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 compensation of Rs.76,800/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 5 X 8/100)
towards loss of future income on the account of disability of the petitioner.
As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as Rs.16,000/- per month, Petitioner is awarded Rs.32,000/- towards loss of earning during laid up period.
30. MEDICAL EXPENSES:-
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment,
Hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied on Ex.P.14-medical bills for Rs.2,42,630/-.
The respondent No.3 has disputed SCCH - 26 19 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 the said bills.
On careful perusal of medical bills at Ex.P.14 reveals that, the petitioner has paid amount towards medicines and treatment.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to medical expenses of Rs.2,42,630/- towards Medical Expenses.
31. By considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion is that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,27,430/-- under the following heads:
Sl. Compensation heads Compensation No. amount 1. Loss of future earning Rs. 76,800/-
capacity due to permanent disability 2.
Towards Pain and Sufferings Rs. 40,000 /-
3. Towards loss of Amenities Rs. 30,000/-
4. Towards attendant, food Rs. 6,000/-
and nourishment and conveyance charges 5.
Towards loss of income Rs. 32,000/-
during laid up period and rest period
6. Towards medical expenses Rs. 2,42,630/-
 TOTAL
Hence, both the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to the compensation to the Petitioner.
However, the respondent No.3 being the insurer of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EW-6696 is liable to pay compensation Rs. 4,27,430/-
with 6% interest to the petitioner from the date of petition till deposit the amount.
35. ISSUE No.3: in view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for  SCCH - 26 21 M.V.C.No.7245/2023 compensation of Rs. 4,27,430/- (Rupees four lakhs twenty seven thousand four hundred and thirty Only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 & 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the respondent No.3 being insurer of offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 51-EW-6696 is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount, release the entire amount to the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
